chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Sayf ibn Umayrih, on the authority of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Doing good is only valued by those who are honorable or religious.

key_terms.ذِي حَسَبٍ: One of noble lineage or status

ai.seo_question: What qualities make a good deed accepted according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to clarify that the social value of a good deed (sani'ah) is contingent upon the doer's standing in either noble lineage (hasab) or religious piety (din). This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between social status and spiritual merit in determining the reception of one's actions within the community.
